# vk 0.13.0 — Hardware qualification and association indexing

Development release, 2026-11-13. Cargo package **`vkrust 0.13.0+1.4.365`**,
Rust library/import name **`vk`**, Git tag **`v0.13.0`**, MIT licensed.
The `+1.4.365` suffix identifies the pinned Vulkan header snapshot, not a
Vulkan 1.4 driver requirement.

[Developer guide](https://dev.realm.software/vk) ·
[Rust API reference](https://docs.rs/vkrust/latest/vk/) ·
[Realm](https://realm.software/)

## Hardware qualification

This is the first release carrying a physical-hardware record instead of
synthetic fixtures alone. On a Microsoft Surface Laptop 5 (Intel Core
i7-1265U, Iris Xe Alder Lake GT2, Mesa/vulkan-intel 26.2.7, Vulkan 1.4.354
device, loader and validation layer 1.4.363), separate Khronos core and
synchronization-validation runs each passed all 32 named native profiles with
no skips, warnings, errors, VUIDs or synchronization hazards. Coverage includes
instance/device/feature operations, timeline semaphores and buffer device
address; compute/fence/readback and descriptor templates; separate, default,
custom, automatic and linear pool storage plus image and mixed-resource pools;
end-to-end defragmentation with GPU copies, relocation commits, multi-pass
Extensive moves, intra-block Balanced/Full compaction, alias-group recreation
and post-commit descriptor rebind; serialized and parallel host mapping and
binding; and OPAQUE_FD/DMA-BUF imports. An offscreen Vulkan 1.3 dynamic
rendering oracle drew and read back a checked triangle under synchronization
validation. This is not WSI, presentation or Vulkan conformance evidence.

## Comparative benchmarks

The new optional `sdk/` workspace builds fresh-process timing consumers
against Ash `0.38.0+1.3.281`, pinned C++ VMA 3.4.0 and checked Vulkano 0.35.2,
outside the package's dependency and workspace boundary. On the same device,
paired medians place loader and device creation at parity with Ash and the
memory-properties query at 1.52x. The allocator remains slower than VMA on
native creation: pooled create/allocate/bind 2.04x and separate
create/allocate/bind 2.10x, with separate destroy/free near parity (1.06x)
and pooled destroy/free at 1.23x. Host-only virtual placement shows 2.05x
combined. Against Vulkano's managed API, pooled placement is 1.53x slower
while separate storage is approximately 4.1x faster combined. Instance
creation measured bimodally on both backends under the session driver state
and is excluded as evidence. See the
[Surface Laptop 5 baseline](../benchmarks/surface-laptop-5-2026-11-13.md) for
the full methodology, environment and retained artifacts.

## Allocator association indexing

Managed resource association checks previously walked every live allocation
on each create/bind, making a pooled batch superlinear in live count. A
per-allocator raw-handle index now carries one owner slot per disjoint image
plane, mirroring the synchronized owner registry; partitioned children record
pending binds locally while committed claims publish into shared scope state.
The pooled operation is flat across 64–2,048 live allocations on the same
harness. The remaining create-side gap versus VMA is constant host
bookkeeping, not live-count-dependent work.

## Status

The experimental designation is removed. The scope statement is unchanged:
full VMA equivalence, wider concurrent stress, multi-driver execution and
additional platforms remain unqualified, and the measured create-side
regression above remains open. See the
[qualification report](../qualification.md) for exact limits.

## Evidence and limits

The workspace test suite passed 3,454 tests including allocator, pool,
synchronization, import, defragmentation and callback-failure fixtures; 53
native profiles ran on the physical device. Formatting, strict
workspace/all-target/all-feature Clippy, strict rustdoc and native-name
search checks passed.

Release CI gates publication on the exact sanitized snapshot's configured
Linux, macOS and Windows tests, extracted-crate/consumer proofs, pinned C
ABI/PFN and VMA comparisons, and explicit software-Vulkan profiles. The CI
run and release assets own the exact release rerun evidence.
